name: Apache Doris
workload: SSB, TPC-H, and TPC-DS analytical benchmarks at sf1000 scale (13/22/99 queries respectively); also cites 100M-row agent-observability workloads vs DuckDB
claimed_speedup: SSB: 11.6s vs ClickHouse 82.2s (~7x); TPC-H: 53.8s vs 279.0s (~5.2x); TPC-DS: 173.8s vs 1913.9s (~11x); page also claims up to 3,135x-7,118x vs DuckDB on 'analytics rollups'/'semi-structured payload' observability workloads (implausible, see caveats)
tradeoffs: MPP distributed OLAP database (Java query planner/FE + C++ vectorized backend/BE), not an embeddable C++ library; heavier operational footprint than DuckDB; same architectural lineage as StarRocks
caveats: First-party benchmark page states no CPU model or compiler/flags; several 'agent observability' multipliers (up to 7,118x vs DuckDB) exceed the 50x plausibility threshold and likely reflect very different query/data shapes rather than an apples-to-apples run, so tier capped at C
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos "OLAP engine" language:C++ --sort stars; benchmark page opened via WebFetch https://doris.apache.org/why-doris/benchmarks/

name: GenDB
workload: TPC-H-derived queries and a leakage-resistant SEC-EDGAR/SQLSmith query set; LLM agent (Claude Code) synthesizes instance-optimized C++ query execution code per query/dataset/hardware, compared against DuckDB, Umbra, MonetDB, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL
claimed_speedup: 214ms total across 5 representative queries vs DuckDB 594ms and Umbra 590ms (2.8x faster than both, the two fastest baselines); another query 6.1x faster than DuckDB (38ms); a separate query drops from 594ms to 74ms after 1 optimization iteration (163x) and others show 12-13x gains over iterations
hardware: 2x Intel Xeon Gold 5218 CPUs, 2.3GHz, 32 physical cores (stated in paper)
tradeoffs: Generates a bespoke C++ execution program per query/workload/hardware via an LLM agent rather than being one general-purpose engine; synthesis has its own latency/cost the headline numbers don't include; early research prototype (paper: Lao & Trummer, 2026, arXiv:2603.02081)
caveats: First-party benchmark from the paper's own repo; hardware is stated but compiler/optimization flags are not, so tier is capped at C rather than A/B; the largest multipliers (up to 163x) come from iterative multi-round self-optimization, not a single fixed run
found_via: arXiv: search abs:DuckDB sortBy=submittedDate,order=descending, then followed citation from JetStream (arXiv:2608.22476) to GenDB's own paper and linked GitHub repo

name: Bespoke OLAP
workload: TPC-H and CEB (Cardinality Estimation Benchmark) query suites; fully autonomous LLM synthesis pipeline builds a workload-specific C++ database engine from scratch, compared multi-threaded against DuckDB and single-threaded against Umbra
claimed_speedup: 11.17x lower total runtime on TPC-H and 45.33x on CEB vs DuckDB (multi-threaded); 7.24x (TPC-H) and 9.56x (CEB) vs Umbra (single-threaded); per-query range 2.83x-102x on TPC-H and 11.6x-1500x on CEB
hardware: AMD EPYC 9654P 96-core processor, 768GB RAM (stated in paper)
stars_or_usage: 50 stars (main repo); companion artifacts repo https://github.com/DataManagementLab/BespokeOLAP_Artifacts has 7 stars
tradeoffs: Synthesizes one engine per fixed workload ('one-size-fits-one'); not usable as a drop-in general-purpose replacement for DuckDB; per-query speedup is highly variable (as low as 2.83x, as high as 1500x)
caveats: GitHub repo is archived (read-only) even though last pushed 2026-07-22, so tagged abandoned per repo status; compiler/flags not stated in paper; some per-query multipliers (up to 1500x on CEB) exceed the 50x plausibility threshold even though the aggregate 11-45x figures look defensible — tier capped at C
found_via: arXiv: cited as prior work by JetStream (arXiv:2608.22476); own paper arXiv:2603.02001 with linked GitHub repos

name: JetStream
workload: TPC-H at SF=20 with periodic refreshes, plus a leakage-resistant SEC-EDGAR (SF=3) workload; an agentic pipeline generates query-specific accelerators (optionally with persistent auxiliary state) that extend an existing DBMS
claimed_speedup: 833x geomean read-only speedup over DuckDB on TPC-H SF=20 with stateful accelerators (vs 34.07x for GenDB and 12.35x for Bespoke OLAP on the same setup); 375x geomean under refreshes every 60s; stateless accelerators (no persistent state) only 1.99x over single-threaded DuckDB; 102x over DuckDB and 486x over PostgreSQL on unseen SEC-EDGAR workload
hardware: dual-socket Intel Xeon Gold 6230 CPUs (40 physical cores, 80 threads), 376GB RAM (stated in paper)
tradeoffs: Headline number depends on precomputed, query-specific auxiliary state (materialized statistics/range trees), not general query acceleration; drops to a much more modest 1.99x with no persistent state allowed; no public code repository found
caveats: 833x/102x/486x are geomeans over generated, workload-specific accelerators, not a general-purpose engine replacement; the ratio far exceeds the 50x plausibility threshold so tier is capped at C; arXiv preprint (MIT CSAIL authors incl. Tim Kraska), not confirmed peer-reviewed; no GitHub/code link found on the arXiv page or in the PDF
